Supports fundamental engineering research on the rates and mechanisms of chemical reactions, systems engineering, and molecular thermodynamics as they relate to the design and optimization of chemical reactors and the production of specialized materials. The Process Systems, Reaction Engineering, and Molecular Thermodynamics program is part of the Chemical Process Systems cluster, which also includes: 1) the Catalysis program; 2) the Electrochemical Systems program; and 3) the Interfacial Engineering program. The goal of the Process Systems, Reaction Engineering, and Molecular Thermodynamics program is to advance fundamental engineering research on the rates and mechanisms of chemical reactions, systems engineering, and molecular thermodynamics as they relate to the design and optimization of chemical reactors and the production of specialized materials that have important impacts on society. The program supports the development of advanced optimization and control algorithms for chemical processes, molecular and multi-scale modeling of complex chemical systems, fundamental studies on molecular thermodynamics, and the integration of these methods and concepts into the design of novel chemical products and manufacturing processes. This program supports sustainable chemical manufacturing research on the development of energy-efficient chemical processes and environmentally-friendly chemical products through concurrent chemical product/process design methods. Sustainability is also enhanced by research that promotes the electrification of the chemical process industries over current thermally-activated processes. Supports experimental and applied computational physical chemistry research on the nature of chemical structure and bonding, electronic structure and chemical dynamics. Supports experimental and applied computational physical chemistry research on the nature of chemical structure and bonding, electronic structure and chemical dynamics. The Chemical Structure and Dynamics (CSD) program supports research projects that advance foundational knowledge on the nature of chemical structure and bonding, electronic structure, and chemical dynamics. At coarse resolution, the CSD Program encompasses the sub-disciplines of experimental physical chemistry and applied computational physical chemistry, and it is interested in projects that enable physical phenomena to be viewed in a new light or in ways that challenge current paradigms. To that end, projects of interest to CSD often rely heavily on the use and/or advancement of sophisticated experimental techniques (e.g., state-selective methods, time and frequency domain spectroscopies, microscopies, single-molecule methods, scattering and diffraction approaches, and surface characterization techniques) or the development of new analysis approaches to further physical understanding. The chemical systems studied range in complexity and include isolated molecules and molecular ions, liquids, clusters, surfaces and interfaces, molecular assemblies and films, nanoscale systems, and biological structures. The CSD Program also supports applied computational chemistry that demonstrates strong synergy with experiment. Investigators who plan to submit proposals on primarily computational projects are advised that their proposals will be reviewed by experimentalists and experts in computational chemistry. The CSD program also encourages proposal submissions in the following topical areas: The CSD Program is interested in projects that would advance our understanding of key Quantum Information Science (QIS) concepts (e.g., coherence, quantum correlations, entanglement) in chemical systems or use QIS concepts to probe chemical structure and dynamics in new ways. Proposals developing new ways of creating, observing, and quantifying these phenomena in electronic, vibrational, and/or rotational quantum states or exploring their role in chemical reactions are of interest. Proposals that leverage artificial intelligence (AI) methods in the design of experimental protocols, and/or the data analysis are welcomed. Grant Opportunities for Academic Liaison with Industry (GOALI) proposals, where such advances are connected directly to industrial considerations, are also encouraged. The CSD program encourages PIs to monitor current funding priorities identified by the Foundation and to highlight relevant synergies in their project summaries and project descriptions. Principal Investigators uncertain of the suitability of their proposals for the CSD Program and of their synergy with other funding priorities and/or programs are strongly encouraged to contact the CSD Program Officers Proposals to the CSD program are welcome at any time, starting September 1, 2026. All proposals submitted to this program (including individual and collaborative proposals, GOALIs) must be submitted to the MPS Chemistry Research Programs Notice of Funding Opportunity (NSF 26-519), except for: RUI proposals must be submitted to the Facilitating Research at Predominantly Undergraduate Institutions: (RUI and ROA-PUI) program. Proposals submitted in response to another solicitation should follow the solicitation guidelines (e.g., CAREER). Early-concept Grants for Exploratory Research (EAGER), Rapid Response Research (RAPID), or Research Advanced by Interdisciplinary Science and Engineering (RAISE) proposals must be discussed with a program officer before submission and then should only be submitted as instructed. MPS Chemistry occasionally supports forward-looking workshops to inform future research needs and directions relevant to chemical science. We are not generally able to support research symposia, including those at either special or recurring meetings and conferences. Workshop proposals must be discussed with a program officer before submission. For recent awards made by the program, search the NSF award database with the Program Element Code 910100. These achievements lie at the confluence of mathematics, statistics, engineering and computer science, yet a clear explanation of the remarkable power and also the limitations of such AI systems has eluded scientists from all disciplines. Critical foundational gaps remain that, if not properly addressed, will soon limit advances in machine learning, curbing progress in artificial intelligence. The National Science Foundation Directorates for Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS), Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE), Engineering (ENG), and Social, Behavioral and Economic Sciences (SBE) will jointly sponsor research collaborations consisting of mathematicians, statisticians, computer scientists, engineers, and social and behavioral scientists focused on the mathematical and theoretical foundations of AI. Research activities should focus on the most challenging mathematical and theoretical questions aimed at understanding the capabilities, limitations, and emerging properties of AI methods as well as the development of novel, and mathematically grounded, design and analysis principles for the current and next generation of AI approaches. Recognizing the importance of international collaborations in promoting scientific discoveries, the National Science Foundation (NSF) and the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (German Research Foundation, DFG) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on research cooperation. The MoU provides an overarching framework to enhance opportunities for collaborative activities between US and German research communities and sets out the principles by which jointly supported activities might be developed. To facilitate the support of collaborative work between US researchers and their German counterparts under this MoU, the Division of Chemistry (CHE) and the Division of Chemical, Bioengineering, Environmental and Transport Systems (CBET) at NSF and the Divisions of Physics and Chemistry (PC) and Engineering Sciences (ING 1) at DFG are pleased to announce a Lead Agency Opportunity for Collaborative Research in Chemistry and Chemical Process and Transport Systems. The goal of this Lead Agency Opportunity is to reduce barriers to working internationally by allowing US and German researchers to submit a single collaborative proposal that will undergo a single review process while funding organizations maintain budgetary control over their awards. Proposals eligible for funding consideration through this Lead Agency Opportunity should review the CHE, CBET, PC, and ING 1 program descriptions for research supported through these divisions/organizations. Proposals are expected to adhere to typical proposal budgets and durations for the relevant CHE, CBET, PC, and ING 1 programs from which funding is sought. A list of participating NSF programs can be found at: https://www.nsf.gov/od/oise/IntlCollaborations/Germany.jsp. German researchers are invited to read: www.dfg.de/nsf-che-cbet. Proposals submitted under this Opportunity will be reviewed by either NSF or DFG as the Lead Agency, depending on where the largest proportion of research lies. Proposals must provide a clear rationale for the need for a US-German collaboration, including the unique expertise and synergy that the collaborating groups will bring to the project. The result of the review process will be shared among the appropriate divisions (NSF/CHE and/or NSF/CBET, and DFG/PC and/or DFG/ING 1) before making final recommendations. All general NSF inquiries should be sent to NSFDFG@nsf.gov. All general DFG inquiries should be sent to NSF-DFG-Chemistry@dfg.de. Submission deadlines vary by program and proposals must meet program-specific requirements to be considered for review. This funding amount is approximate and is subject to availability of funds. The overall funding for the program is established independently by each participating division. Estimated program budget, number of awards and average award size/duration are subject to the availability of funds. Average award size and duration (varies with different participating program limits) are subject to the availability of funds. A US individual may appear as Principal Investigator (PI), co-PI, or senior/key personnel on only one proposal per annual cycle submitted in response to this solicitation. For programs with no submission deadline, the 12-month cycle starts with the proposal submission date. For proposals submitted to NSF/CHE, the submission will count towards the total proposal submission limit to the Disciplinary Research Programs (DRP), as defined in NSF CHE-DRP and CHE-DRP:NDP solicitations. For German Personnel, there is no limitation. If a US individual is listed as PI, co-PI, or senior/key personnel on more than one proposal to this solicitation, then only the first submitted proposal will be considered. The remaining submission(s) will be returned without review. Randolph Building 401 Dulany Street Alexandria, VA 22314 Sign up for email updates

Supports interdisciplinary research and education to develop a secure, resilient and trustworthy global cyber ecosystem by addressing vulnerabilities, improving trust in cyber systems and cultivating a well-trained cybersecurity workforce. Our world is at a pivotal moment where the boundaries dividing the physical and social worlds from the cyber world have become blurred. Cyberspace has evolved from an interconnected digital environment into a complex and interdependent cyber ecosystem that involves hardware, software, networks, data, people, organizations, countries, and the physical world. Critical functions of everyday life are deeply intertwined with computing, including health, government, commerce, the public sphere, education, critical infrastructure, interpersonal communication, and transportation. The complexity and inter-dependencies in cyberspace can be misused and exploited by malicious actors. These in turn can trigger adverse outcomes such as disruption of critical infrastructure and systems; theft of intellectual property and sensitive data; amplification of inequalities; disclosure of private information of individuals, organizations, and governments; and threats to lives, livelihoods, and reputations. Furthermore, constant attacks on the data and assets of corporations, governments, and individuals undermine people’s trust in decision-making and processes that depend critically on these cyber systems. The Security, Privacy, and Trust in Cyberspace (SaTC 2.0) program aims to build trust in global cyber ecosystems. Trust is the core tenet of this program and, for the purposes of this solicitation, is broadly defined to include our confidence in the security, privacy, and resilience of cyberspace, particularly in the face of malicious intent. Achieving this level of confidence in cyberspace requires not only understanding the vulnerabilities in a system that could be exploited and how they can be addressed, but also understanding the social and technical dimensions of trust in cyber systems, along with the educational efforts needed to increase public awareness of risks in cyberspace, and building a well-trained corps of privacy and security professionals. SaTC 2.0 spans the interests of NSF's Directorates for Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE), Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS), Social, Behavioral and Economic Sciences (SBE), and STEM Education (EDU). Supports research on living systems at the molecular, subcellular and cellular levels. Core areas supported include cellular dynamics and function; genetic mechanisms; molecular biophysics; and systems and synthetic biology. MCB supports research that promises to uncover the fundamental properties of living systems across atomic, molecular, subcellular, and cellular scales. The program gives high priority to projects that advance mechanistic understanding of the structure, function, and evolution of molecular, subcellular, and cellular systems, especially research that aims at quantitative and predictive knowledge of complex behavior and emergent properties. MCB encourages research exploring new concepts in molecular and cellular biology, while incorporating insights and approaches from other scientific disciplines, such as chemistry, computer science, engineering, mathematics, and physics, to illuminate principles that govern life at the molecular and cellular level. MCB also encourages research that exploits experimental and theoretical approaches and utilizes a diverse spectrum of model and non-model animals, plants, and microbes across the tree of life. Proposals that pursue potentially transformative ideas are welcome, even if these entail higher risk. This solicitation calls for proposals in research areas supported by the four MCB core clusters, including: (i) structure, dynamics, and function of biomolecules and supramolecular assemblies, especially under physiological conditions (Molecular Biophysics); (ii) organization, processing, expression, regulation, and evolution of genetic and epigenetic information (Genetic Mechanisms); (iii) cellular structure, properties, and function across broad spatiotemporal scales (Cellular Dynamics and Function); and (iv) systems and/or synthetic biology to study complex interactions through modeling or manipulation or design of living systems at the molecular-to-cellular scale (Systems and Synthetic Biology). All MCB clusters prioritize projects that integrate across scales, investigate molecular and cellular evolution, synergize experimental research with computational or mathematical modeling, and/or develop innovative, broadly applicable methods and technologies. Projects that bridge the intellectual edges between MCB clusters are welcome. Projects that integrate molecular and cellular biosciences with other subdisciplines of biology are also welcome through the new Integrative Research in Biology (IntBIO) track. Regarding health-related challenges, NSF supports basic research in all areas of the biological sciences and recognizes that this foundational research is likely to impact many different areas, including human health. MCB celebrates all the biological science discoveries funded through MCB awards that have had major impacts on health, environment, energy, food production, and other applications. Nevertheless, research focused exclusively on understanding human diseases and their treatment is normally outside of the scope of funding and will be returned without review unless that research significantly advances other fields such as engineering, computer science, or the mathematical and physical sciences. The objective of the Human-Environment and Geographical Sciences Program is to support basic scientific research about the nature, causes, consequences, or evolution of the spatial dimensions of human behaviors, activities, and dynamics as well as their interactions with environmental and social processes across a range of scales. Contemporary geographical research encompasses diverse research traditions and methodologies. Recognizing the breadth of the field’s contributions to science, the HEGS Program welcomes proposals for empirically grounded, theoretically engaged, methodologically rigorous, and generalizable research that advances geographical and geospatial sciences. Because the National Science Foundation's mandate is to support fundamental scientific research, the HEGS program cannot fund research that takes as its primary goal humanistic interpretations or findings that are not generalizable or reproducible. HEGS welcomes proposals that utilize quantitative, qualitative, or mixed methods in novel ways. However, a proposal that applies geographical or geospatial methods to a geographic problem without proposing how that problem provides an opportunity to make a theory-testing or theory-expanding contribution to geographical science, broadly defined, will be returned without review. HEGS supported projects are expected to yield results that will enhance, expand, and transform fundamental geographical theory and geospatial methods and that will have broader impacts that benefit society. Generally, successful HEGS proposals should describe clear and detailed plans for data collection (including sample selection if appropriate), justification for proposed methods, plans for data analysis, attention to confounding variables, and efforts to address biases (e.g., confirmatory biases, selection biases, etc.). Competitive HEGS proposals should substantiate the validity of findings and generalizability to broader contexts. It should be noted that HEGS is situated in the Behavioral and Cognitive Sciences Division of the Social, Behavioral and Economic Sciences Directorate at NSF. Therefore, it is critical that research projects submitted to the HEGS program illustrate how the proposed research questions engage human dimensions that are relevant and important to people and societies. A proposal that fails to be responsive to these program expectations will be returned without review. General inquiries should be submitted to HEGS-info@nsf.gov. Supports research on the theory of algorithms focused on problems that are central to computer science and engineering, and the development of new algorithms and techniques for analyzing algorithms and computational complexity. The Algorithmic Foundations (AF) program supports potentially transformative projects in the theory of algorithms. Projects should be characterized by algorithmic innovation accompanied by rigorous analysis. Of interest is research on algorithms for problems that are central to computer science and engineering, as well as new techniques for the rigorous analysis of algorithms and computational complexity. AF supports theoretical research that bounds the intrinsic difficulty of problems to determine measures of complexity in formal models of computation, classical or new. The goal is to understand the fundamental limits of resource-bounded computation and to obtain efficient algorithms operating within those limits. Research on resources other than the traditional time and space measures, such as communication and energy, is also encouraged, as is research on tradeoffs between resource use and solution quality, such as running time vs. approximation error. Rigorous analysis of properties of algorithms relating to fairness, ethics, accountability, transparency, and privacy is also in scope. In addition to the traditional sequential-computing paradigm, AF supports research on the design and analysis of novel algorithms in parallel and distributed models, as well as computational models and algorithms that capture essential aspects of computing over massive data sets. New techniques for the design and analysis of algorithms and analysis of problem complexity in areas such as optimization, cryptography, computational geometry, game theory and economics, social networks, machine learning, and numeric, symbolic, and algebraic computing are within the scope of this program. The program also supports research in algorithms needed in applied areas of research, including algorithmic research on problems arising in other areas of research on computing. While relevance to application areas is important and collaboration with researchers in these areas is encouraged, research funded by this program must advance the theoretical study of algorithms. When accompanying rigorous analysis of computational resource requirements and/or algorithmic performance measures, implementation efforts and empirical evaluation are considered strong broader impacts. Letters of collaboration from applied researchers are encouraged. Emerging topics such as quantum computing and biological models of computation are now addressed in the Foundations of Emerging Technologies (FET) program. However, projects in these areas focused on foundational issues of algorithms and complexity in these topics, as described above, can also be considered by the AF program. Supports the development of genomic tools and research to uncover the relationships between genes and phenotypes across environmental, developmental, social and genomic contexts. Through the Enabling Discovery through GEnomics (EDGE) program, the National Science Foundation (NSF) and the National Institutes for Health (NIH) support research to advance understanding of comparative and functional genomics. The EDGE program supports the development of innovative tools, technologies, resources, and infrastructure that advance biological research focused on the identification of the causal mechanisms connecting genes and phenotypes. The EDGE program also supports functional genomic research that addresses the mechanistic basis of complex traits in diverse organisms within the context (environmental, developmental, social, and/or genomic) in which they function. These goals are essential to uncovering the rules that underlie genomes-to-phenomes relationships and predict phenotype, an area relevant to Understanding the Rules of Life: Predicting Phenotype, one of the 10 Big Ideas for NSF investment. The goals also support the NHGRI priority to establish the roles and relationships of all genes and regulatory elements in pathways, networks, and phenotypes. General inquiries regarding this program should be made to: BIOEDGE@NSF.GOV For questions about NHGRI interests, contact: National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI) NHGRI will support the development of resources, approaches, and technologies that will accelerate genomic research on the structure of genomes, the biology of genomes, and the biology of disease; that will use genomics to advance the science of medicine; and that will incorporate genomics to improve the effectiveness of healthcare. NHGRI will also support genomic research in several cross-cutting areas, including the ethical, legal and societal implications of genomics and genetics research, bioinformatics, technology development, and research training and career development. In general, NHGRI supports studies that provide generalizable methods and knowledge. Applications for studies relevant only to a particular disease or organ system should be directed to the appropriate Institute or Center. Supports research on the ecological, evolutionary, organismal and social drivers that influence infectious diseases and increase quantitative and/or computational understanding of pathogen transmission dynamics. The multi-agency Ecology and Evolution of Infectious Diseases program supports research on the ecological, evolutionary, organismal, and social drivers that influence the transmission dynamics of infectious diseases. The central theme of submitted projects must be the quantitative, mathematical, or computational understanding of pathogen transmission dynamics. The intent is discovery of principles of infectious disease (re)emergence and transmission and testing mathematical or computational models that elucidate infectious disease systems. Projects should be broad, interdisciplinary efforts that go beyond the scope of typical studies. They should focus on the determinants and interactions of (re)emergence and transmission among any host species, including but not limited to humans, non-human animals, and/or plants. This includes, for example, the spread of pathogens; the influence of environmental factors such as climate; the population dynamics and genetics of vectors and reservoir species or hosts; how the physiology or behavior of the pathogen, vector, or host species biology affects transmission dynamics; the feedback between ecological transmission and evolutionary dynamics; and the cultural, social, behavioral, and economic dimensions of pathogen transmission and disease. Research may be on zoonotic, environmentally-borne, vector-borne, enteric, or respiratory pathogens of either terrestrial, aquatic, or marine systems and organisms, including diseases of animals and plants, at any scale from specific pathogens to inclusive environmental systems. Proposals for research on disease systems of public health concern to Low- or Middle-Income Countries (LMICs) are strongly encouraged, as are disease systems of concern in agricultural systems. Investigators are encouraged to develop the appropriate multidisciplinary team, including for example, anthropologists, modelers, ecologists, bioinformaticians, genomics researchers, social scientists, economists, oceanographers, mathematical scientists, behaviorists, epidemiologists, evolutionary biologists, entomologists, immunologists, parasitologists, microbiologists, bacteriologists, virologists, pathologists or veterinarians, with the goal of integrating knowledge across disciplines to enhance our ability to predict and control infectious diseases. The Communications and Information Foundations (CIF) program supports research activities that address the theoretical underpinnings for information acquisition, transmission, and processing in communications and information processing systems. CIF projects have contributed to the development of the inter-related areas of communications, information theory, coding theory, and signal and image processing, areas that are expected to play key roles in future technology. The CIF program also supports foundational research in networked systems, such as network information theory and cross-layer design in wireless systems. Examples include secure communication, sensor networks, and other scenarios that feature massive data aggregation from distributed sensing. In addition to the traditional topics that have fueled the information revolution, there is continued interest within the CIF program in new paradigms. These include but are not limited to statistical learning and inference, signal processing on graphs and networks, multi-terminal communication problems, information-theoretic security, geometric methods in signal processing and machine learning, computational imaging, and communication-theoretic challenges associated with emerging communication technology. In the machine learning area in particular, CIF seeks to encourage research promoting paradigms based on foundational principles, rooted in information theory and statistical inference, that advance the explainability and generalizability of machine learning. Topics of interest include, but are not limited to, scalability, performance guarantees, and fundamental limits, alongside fairness and robustness of machine learning techniques. At its core, CIF is interested in the mathematical exploration of novel problem formulations rooted in the aforementioned application domains. Supports fundamental research on the design of engineered artifacts — devices, products, processes, platforms, materials, organizations, systems and systems of systems. DEB encourages research that elucidates fundamental principles that identify and explain the unity and diversity of life and its interactions with the environment over space and time. descricao_completa: A chamada tem por objetivo selecionar projetos de P,D&I apresentados por ICTs públicas e privadas para desenvolvimento de soluções tecnológicas voltadas à agricultura familiar brasileira, obrigatoriamente em parceria com cooperativas da agricultura familiar. Orçamento total R$ 100 milhões em recursos não reembolsáveis do FNDCT/CT-Agro. Pelo menos 30% dos recursos deverão ser destinados às regiões Norte, Nordeste e Centro-Oeste, desde que existam projetos meritórios. Linhas Temáticas 1- Comercialização, acesso a mercados e logística cooperativa. 2 - Desenvolvimento de cadeias produtivas e agroindustrialização cooperativa. 3 - Gestão da inovação, transformação digital e absorção tecnológica. 4 - Economia circular. 5 - Eficiência energética e resiliência climática. Quem Pode Participar São elegíveis ICTs públicas e privadas com experiência comprovada em: pesquisa; desenvolvimento tecnológico; extensão tecnológica; transferência de tecnologia; capacitação ou assistência tecnológica voltadas à agricultura familiar ou ao PNRA. Exigência Central do Edital A ICT deve comprovar parceria formal prévia com pelo menos uma cooperativa da agricultura familiar estabelecida há pelo menos 1 ano antes da publicação do edital. Além disso: a cooperativa deve possuir CAF ativo; e pelo menos 70% dos cooperados devem possuir CAF Pessoa Física ativo. A comprovação deve ocorrer mediante instrumento jurídico válido, contendo identificação das partes, assinaturas e vigência mínima de um ano. Características dos Projetos - Valor solicitado Mínimo: R$ 3 milhões. Máximo: R$ 15 milhões. - Prazo: Até 36 meses. - Maturidade Tecnológica: O projeto deve partir de TRL 3 ou superior. Esse é um critério eliminatório tanto na habilitação quanto na avaliação de mérito. - Participação Cada ICT pode apresentar apenas uma proposta como executora principal. Pode participar de outras propostas como coexecutora. A proposta deve incluir, entre outros: - Carta de Manifestação de Interesse da Cooperativa. - Extrato CAF Pessoa Jurídica. - Documento que demonstre a parceria prévia de 1 ano. - Política de Inovação (para ICTs públicas). - Relação da equipe vinculada ao cronograma físico. - Justificativa do TRL inicial e final. - Metodologia detalhada. - Avaliação dos riscos tecnológicos. titulo: MSCA postdoctorale beurzen 2027
descricao_resumida: Financiamento para pós-doutores excelentes que buscam mobilidade internacional, com duração de 12 a 24 meses, para projetos de investigação em países associados ao Horizon Europa ou terceiros não associados. Oferecimento de bolsas para investigadores de todas as nacionalidades, incluindo Global Postdoctoral Fellowships para cidadãos europeus. Apoio a investigação em áreas de inovação e ciência aberta, com possibilidade de detachment até 50% da duração do projeto.
descricao_completa: Verwacht resultaat: De projectresultaten zullen naar verwachting bijdragen tot de volgende resultaten: Voor ondersteunde postdoctorale fellows meer onderzoek en overdraagbare vaardigheden en competenties, wat leidt tot een betere inzetbaarheid en loopbaanperspectieven van postdoctorale MSCA-bursalen binnen de academische wereld en daarbuiten; Nieuwe denkrichtingen en benaderingen voor O&O;Ik werk gesmeed door internationale, intersectorale en interdisciplinaire ervaring; Verbeterde netwerk- en communicatiecapaciteiten met wetenschappelijke collega's en met het grote publiek, die het effect van onderzoek en innovatie zullen vergroten en verbreden. Voor deelnemende organisaties betere afstemming van de arbeidsvoorwaarden voor onderzoekers overeenkomstig de beginselen van het Europees Handvest voor Onderzoekers; Verbetering van de kwaliteit en duurzaamheid van onderzoeksopleiding en -toezicht; grotere mondiale aantrekkelijkheid, zichtbaarheid en reputatie van de deelnemende organisatie(s); Sterkere O&I-capaciteit en -output bij deelnemende organisaties; betere kennisoverdracht; Regelmatige feedback van onderzoeksresultaten over onderwijs en educatie bij deelnemende organisaties. Toepassingsgebied: Er zullen beurzen worden verstrekt aan excellente onderzoekers die zich bezighouden met internationale mobiliteit. Aanvragen worden gezamenlijk ingediend door de onderzoeker en een begunstigde in de academische of niet-academische sector. Postdoctorale beurzen kunnen plaatsvinden in Europa (d.w.z. in een EU-lidstaat of een met Horizon Europa geassocieerd land) of in een niet met Horizon Europa geassocieerd derde land: Europese postdoctorale beurzen staan open voor onderzoekers van elke nationaliteit die aan O&O-projecten willen deelnemen door vanuit elk land ter wereld naar Europa te komen of zich binnen Europa te verplaatsen. De standaardduur van deze beurzen moet tussen de 12 en 24 maanden liggen. Global Postdoctoral Fellowships staan open voor Europese onderdanen of langdurig ingezetenen [1] die willen deelnemen aan R&I-projecten met organisaties buiten de EU-lidstaten en met Horizon Europa geassocieerde landen. Deze beurzen vereisen een uitgaande fase van minimaal 12 en maximaal 24 maanden in een niet-geassocieerd derde land en een verplichte terugkeerfase van 12 maanden naar een gastorganisatie die gevestigd is in een EU-lidstaat of een met Horizon Europa geassocieerd land. Specifieke subsidiabiliteitsvoorwaarden zijn van toepassing op MSCA-postdoctorale beurzen op de onderzoeksgebieden die onder het Euratom-programma voor onderzoek en opleiding [1] vallen. Detacheringen Onderzoekers die een Postdoctoral Fellowship ontvangen, kunnen ervoor kiezen om een detacheringsfase op te nemen, binnen de totale duur van hun fellowship in elk land wereldwijd. De detacheringsfase kan een enkele periode zijn of worden onderverdeeld in kortere mobiliteitsperioden. Voor Europese postdoctorale beurzen mogen detacheringen niet meer bedragen dan de helft van de gevraagde duur van de actie (met uitzondering van de duur van de actie, eventuele extra periodes voor een niet-academische stage) en moeten zij in overeenstemming zijn met de projectdoelstellingen en een aanzienlijke waarde en impact toevoegen aan de beurs. Voor Global Postdoctoral Fellowships zijn optionele detacheringen toegestaan voor maximaal de helft van de uitgaande fase. Maximaal drie maanden van dergelijke detacheringen kunnen aan het begin van het project bij de begunstigde (of geassocieerde partners die met de begunstigde verbonden zijn) worden besteed, zodat de onderzoeker daar tijd kan doorbrengen voordat hij naar de geassocieerde partner in het derde land gaat. Deze periode van maximaal drie maanden wordt beschouwd als onderdeel van de uitgaande fase. Detacheringen kunnen niet plaatsvinden tijdens de verplichte terugkeerperiode van twaalf maanden naar de gastorganisatie in een EU-lidstaat of een met Horizon Europa geassocieerd land. Plaatsingen in de niet-academische sector Postdoctorale beurzen kunnen voorzien in een extra periode van maximaal zes maanden om onderzoekers te ondersteunen die aan het einde van het project kiezen voor een stage om aan O&I-projecten te werken in een organisatie uit de niet-academische sector die in een EU-lidstaat of een met Horizon Europa geassocieerd land is gevestigd [3]. Hoewel deze mogelijkheid ook beschikbaar is voor fellows die zijn aangeworven in de niet-academische sector, moet een dergelijke plaatsing worden uitgevoerd bij een andere niet-academische gastorganisatie die is gevestigd in een EU-lidstaat of een met Horizon Europa geassocieerd land [4]. Het verzoek om een dergelijke niet-academische plaatsing moet integraal deel uitmaken van het voorstel, waarin de meerwaarde voor het project en voor de loopbaanontwikkeling van de onderzoeker wordt toegelicht, en zal worden geëvalueerd. Deze stimulans is bedoeld om loopbaanbewegingen tussen sectoren en organisaties te bevorderen en zo innovatie en kennisoverdracht te stimuleren en tegelijkertijd de carrièremogelijkheden voor onderzoekers uit te breiden. Als de plaatsing niet voldoet aan de vereisten (die plaatsvinden in een academische organisatie of in een derde land), wordt het voorstel beoordeeld zonder rekening te houden met de plaatsing. Dit kan van invloed zijn op de eindscore. Opleidingsactiviteiten De in het kader van de postdoctorale beurzen uitgevoerde opleidingsactiviteiten moeten essentiële overdraagbare vaardigheden en competenties integreren die alle gebieden gemeen hebben, met inbegrip van digitale vaardigheden (bv. generatieve AI), en de cultuur van open wetenschap, kennisvalorisatie [5] en, indien van toepassing, innovatie en ondernemerschap, alsook goed wetenschappelijk gedrag, zoals onderzoeksintegriteit, bevorderen. De postdoctorale beurzen moeten fellows met name in staat stellen een carrière in het onderzoek na te streven en hen adequaat voor te bereiden op intensievere samenwerking op het gebied van onderzoek en informatie-uitwisseling die mogelijk wordt gemaakt door nieuwe (digitale) technologieën (bv. samenwerkingsinstrumenten, openstelling van de toegang tot publicaties en andere onderzoeksresultaten, waaronder gegevens, FAIR-gegevensbeheer, maatschappelijke betrokkenheid en burgerwetenschap, enz.). Loopbaanontwikkelingsplan Om MSCA postdoctorale fellows uit te rusten met vaardigheden die hun carrièremogelijkheden binnen en buiten de academische wereld verbeteren en uitbreiden, moet een loopbaanontwikkelingsplan gezamenlijk worden opgesteld door de supervisor (s) en de onderzoeker. Naast onderzoeksdoelstellingen moet dit plan de opleidings- en loopbaanbehoeften van de onderzoeker omvatten, met inbegrip van opleiding over overdraagbare vaardigheden, onderwijs, planning voor publicaties en deelname aan conferenties en evenementen die gericht zijn op het openstellen van wetenschap en onderzoek voor burgers. Het plan moet aan het begin van de actie als projectproduct worden ingediend en kan zo nodig worden bijgewerkt. Euratom Ter bevordering van nucleaire expertise en excellentie en synergieën tussen programma's komen organisaties die actief zijn op het gebied van nucleair onderzoek en die gevestigd zijn in een van de EU-lidstaten of met het Euratom-programma voor onderzoek en opleiding geassocieerde landen, in aanmerking voor deelname [6]. MSCA-postdoctorale beurzen op dit onderzoeksgebied zullen worden ondersteund door het Euratom-programma voor onderzoek en opleiding door middel van een indicatieve jaarlijkse financiële bijdrage van 1 miljoen EUR aan de oproep tot het indienen van postdoctorale beurzen van MSCA [7]. EOR-beurzen De EOR-beurzen die via bijlage 11 bij het werkprogramma worden uitgevoerd, verbreding van de deelname en versterking van de Europese onderzoeksruimte, bieden specifieke steun aan onderzoekers om hun beurs in een verbredend land te organiseren [8]. Dit zal helpen excellentie te verspreiden en bijdragen aan het bevorderen van een evenwichtige hersencirculatie in verbredende landen. Voor meer richtsnoeren over specifieke gebieden van kennisvalorisatie, zie de praktijkcodes van de Europese Commissie inzake het beheer van intellectuele activa, normalisatie, cocreatie tussen het bedrijfsleven en de academische wereld en burgerbetrokkenheid bij kennisvalorisatie. Als de plaatsing niet voldoet aan de vereisten (die plaatsvinden in een academische organisatie of in een derde land), wordt het voorstel beoordeeld zonder rekening te houden met de plaatsing. titulo: Quantum Benchmarking Initiative expands quest to separate hype from reality
descricao_resumida: Solicitação para organizações não financiadas pelo Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) participarem da nova etapa A do Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBIT), focando em arquiteturas de computação quântica que possam alcançar operação em escala de utilidade até 2033.

Secure .mil websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .mil website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. As the quantum computing field accelerates, DARPA’s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) is expanding to capture its momentum. Organizations that have not yet been funded by QBI are invited to join under a new Stage A Quantum Benchmarking Initiative Topic (QBIT), which builds on QBI’s ongoing effort to rigorously determine whether any quantum computing architecture can achieve utility-scale operation — meaning its computational value exceeds its cost — by 2033. Of particular interest are entrants with distinct approaches that have not yet been evaluated under QBI. Selected participants will enter Stage A, a six-month period in which they will describe a full system concept and provide evidence supporting its feasibility. With this solicitation comes another shift for QBI: Micah Stoutimore is assuming the role of managing director for QBI, succeeding founding program manager Joe Altepeter who will support the transition prior to departing the agency. Stoutimore has served as deputy program manager since the Initiative’s inception and supported related pilot efforts that helped shape the program’s evaluation framework. The transition is in keeping with DARPA tradition of mandatory limited tenure for program managers, a deliberate approach designed to keep programs fresh, continuously challenge assumptions, and ensure a steady infusion of new technical perspectives. In fact, it now seems likely that someone will build a utility-scale quantum computer by 2033, but it remains unclear exactly which team or teams might get across that finish line. – Micah Stoutimore, managing director, Quantum Benchmarking Initiative QBI “Joe built QBI from a concept into the world’s largest evaluation of quantum computing, and I’m grateful for the foundation he established,” said Stoutimore. “I’m honored to take on the role and continue steering the initiative as we expand the range of approaches under examination.” Since its launch in mid-2024, QBI has evaluated approaches from 20 commercial companies spanning a variety of qubit architectures. Eleven organizations have advanced to Stage B for deeper technical risk-reduction and development planning, while two performers from the Underexplored Systems for Utility-Scale Quantum Computing (US2QC) pilot program, have advanced to Stage C, working with the government to verify and validate system-level operation. “Our renewed invitation to join Stage A reflects the rigor with which we evaluate every approach,” said Stoutimore. “Both QBI and the broader quantum computing field have advanced rapidly since our first call. In fact, it now seems likely that someone will build a utility-scale quantum computer by 2033, but it remains unclear exactly which team or teams might get across that finish line. We want to ensure we are assessing every viable pathway.” Abstracts are due July 31, 2026, and full proposals for the Stage A QBIT are due Sept. 30, 2026. Interested parties can find further details within the solicitation on SAM.gov. titulo: MSCA-COFUND 2027
descricao_resumida: Financiamento co-financiado pela UE para programas de doutorado que desenvolvem competências de pesquisa, mobilidade internacional e valorização do conhecimento. O edital visa melhorar recursos humanos em R&I por meio de programas de doutorado em disciplinas de pesquisa, com requisitos de treinamento em competências digitais, carreira e boas práticas científicas. A elegibilidade abrange organizações que proponham programas de doutorado alinhados a estratégias regionais ou nacionais de especialização inteligente.
descricao_completa: Erwartetes Ergebnis: Von den Projektergebnissen wird erwartet, dass sie zu folgenden Ergebnissen beitragen: Für unterstützte Promovierende vertiefte und vielfältigere forschungsbezogene und übertragbare Fähigkeiten und Kompetenzen; Verbesserung der Beschäftigungsfähigkeit und der Karriereaussichten sowohl innerhalb der Wissenschaft als auch darüber hinaus; Neue Denkweisen und Ansätze für R& Ich arbeite geschmiedet durch internationale, sektorübergreifende und interdisziplinäre Erfahrung; Verbesserte Vernetzungs- und Kommunikationskapazitäten mit wissenschaftlichen Kollegen sowie mit der breiten Öffentlichkeit, die die Wirkung von Forschung und Innovation verstärken und ausweiten werden. Für teilnehmende Organisationen Verbesserung der Qualität und Nachhaltigkeit der Forschungsausbildung; Steigerung der globalen Attraktivität, Sichtbarkeit und Reputation der teilnehmenden Organisation(en); Stärkere FuE-Förderung;I-Kapazität und -Output unter den teilnehmenden Organisationen; Erhöhung des Beitrags der teilnehmenden Organisationen zu den lokalen, regionalen und/oder nationalen sozioökonomischen Ökosystemen; Regelmäßiges Feedback von Forschungsergebnissen in Lehre und Ausbildung der teilnehmenden Organisationen. Anwendungsbereich: Die Bewerberinnen und Bewerber reichen Vorschläge für neue oder bestehende Promotionsprogramme ein, die sich auf die Verbesserung der Humanressourcen in R&I auf regionaler, nationaler oder internationaler Ebene auswirken. Diese Programme werden von MSCA COFUND kofinanziert. Die vorgeschlagenen Programme können alle Forschungsdisziplinen abdecken („Bottom-up“), können sich aber ausnahmsweise auch auf bestimmte Disziplinen konzentrieren, insbesondere wenn sie auf nationalen oder regionalen Forschungs- und Innovationsstrategien für intelligente Spezialisierung (RIS3-Strategien) beruhen. In diesem Fall sollte das Spektrum der abgedeckten Disziplinen den Forschern eine angemessene Flexibilität bei der Definition ihres Themas ermöglichen. Die Finanzierung von Synergien mit kohäsionspolitischen Fonds und anderen EU-Finanzierungsquellen wird nachdrücklich gefördert. Ein Karriereentwicklungsplan muss vom Betreuer und jedem rekrutierten Forscher bei der Rekrutierung gemeinsam erstellt werden. Zusätzlich zu den Forschungszielen umfasst dieser Plan den Ausbildungs- und Karrierebedarf des Forschers, einschließlich Schulungen zu übertragbaren Fähigkeiten, Lehre, Planung von Veröffentlichungen und Teilnahme an Konferenzen und Veranstaltungen zur Öffnung von Wissenschaft und Forschung für die Bürger. Der Plan muss zu Beginn der Einstellung erstellt werden und sollte innerhalb von 18 Monaten überarbeitet (und erforderlichenfalls aktualisiert) werden. Doktorandenprogramme bieten Forschungsausbildungsaktivitäten an, die es Doktoranden ermöglichen, ihre Fähigkeiten und Kompetenzen zu entwickeln und zu erweitern. Sie werden zur Verleihung eines Doktortitels in mindestens einem EU-Mitgliedstaat oder einem mit Horizont Europa assoziierten Land führen. Die Ausbildungsmaßnahmen sollten auf den EU-Grundsätzen für innovative Doktorandenausbildung beruhen. Im Rahmen der Doktorandenprogramme sollten umfangreiche Schulungsmodule entwickelt werden, die sich mit den wichtigsten übertragbaren Fähigkeiten und Kompetenzen befassen, die allen Bereichen, einschließlich digitaler Kompetenzen (z. B. generativer KI), gemeinsam sind, und die Kultur der offenen Wissenschaft, die Valorisierung von Wissen [1] und gegebenenfalls Innovation und Unternehmertum sowie gutes wissenschaftliches Verhalten wie Forschungsintegrität fördern. Insbesondere sollten Promotionsprogramme Doktoranden angemessen auf eine Laufbahn in der Forschung vorbereiten und sie angemessen auf eine verstärkte Forschungszusammenarbeit und einen verstärkten Informationsaustausch vorbereiten, die durch neue (digitale) Technologien ermöglicht werden (z. B. kollaborative Instrumente, Öffnung des Zugangs zu Veröffentlichungen und anderen Forschungsergebnissen, einschließlich Daten, FAIR-Datenmanagement, gesellschaftliches Engagement und Bürgerwissenschaft usw.). Zusätzlich zur obligatorischen internationalen Mobilität werden die Antragsteller ermutigt, Elemente der sektorübergreifenden Mobilität und Interdisziplinarität in ihre Programme aufzunehmen. Die Zusammenarbeit mit einem breiteren Spektrum assoziierter Partner, auch aus dem nichtakademischen Sektor, wird bei der Bewertung positiv berücksichtigt. Diese Organisationen können Aufnahme- oder Abordnungsmöglichkeiten oder Ausbildungsmodule in den Bereichen Forschung oder übertragbare Kompetenzen anbieten. Besonderes Augenmerk wird auf die Qualität der Betreuungs- und Mentoring-Regelungen sowie der Berufsberatung gelegt. Das Auswahlverfahren für Doktoranden muss im Einklang mit der Europäischen Charta für Forscher offen, transparent und leistungsorientiert sein. In der Stellenausschreibung (die international, auch auf der EURAXESS [2]-Website, bekannt gemacht werden soll) muss angegeben werden, ob die veröffentlichten Sätze alle Steuern und Beiträge des Arbeitgebers und des Arbeitnehmers enthalten. Wenn möglich, sollte das Bruttogehalt (Nettogehalt + Steuern und Beiträge des Arbeitnehmers) veröffentlicht werden. [1] „Wissensvalorisierung“ ist der Prozess der Schaffung von sozialem und wirtschaftlichem Wert aus Wissen durch die Verknüpfung verschiedener Bereiche und Sektoren und durch die Umwandlung von Daten, Know-how und Forschungsergebnissen in nachhaltige Produkte, Dienstleistungen, Lösungen und wissensbasierte Maßnahmen zum Nutzen der Gesellschaft“ ( EUR-Lex – 32022H2415 – EN – EUR-Lex). Weitere Leitlinien zu bestimmten Bereichen der Valorisierung von Wissen finden sich in den Verhaltenskodizes der Europäischen Kommission zur Verwaltung geistiger Vermögenswerte, zur Normung, zur Ko-Kreation von Industrie und Hochschulen und zur Bürgerbeteiligung bei der Valorisierung von Wissen. [2] https://euraxess.ec.europa.eu/

Insbesondere sollten Promotionsprogramme Doktoranden angemessen auf eine Laufbahn in der Forschung vorbereiten und sie angemessen auf eine verstärkte Forschungszusammenarbeit und einen verstärkten Informationsaustausch vorbereiten, die durch neue (digitale) Technologien ermöglicht werden (z. B. kollaborative Instrumente, Öffnung des Zugangs zu Veröffentlichungen und anderen Forschungsergebnissen, einschließlich Daten, FAIR-Datenmanagement, gesellschaftliches Engagement und Bürgerwissenschaft usw.). Zusätzlich zur obligatorischen internationalen Mobilität werden die Antragsteller ermutigt, Elemente der sektorübergreifenden Mobilität und Interdisziplinarität in ihre Programme aufzunehmen. Die Zusammenarbeit mit einem breiteren Spektrum assoziierter Partner, auch aus dem nichtakademischen Sektor, wird bei der Bewertung positiv berücksichtigt. Diese Organisationen können Aufnahme- oder Abordnungsmöglichkeiten oder Ausbildungsmodule in den Bereichen Forschung oder übertragbare Kompetenzen anbieten. Besonderes Augenmerk wird auf die Qualität der Betreuungs- und Mentoring-Regelungen sowie der Berufsberatung gelegt. Das Auswahlverfahren für Doktoranden muss im Einklang mit der Europäischen Charta für Forscher offen, transparent und leistungsorientiert sein. In der Stellenausschreibung (die international, auch auf der EURAXESS [2]-Website, bekannt gemacht werden soll) muss angegeben werden, ob die veröffentlichten Sätze alle Steuern und Beiträge des Arbeitgebers und des Arbeitnehmers enthalten. Wenn möglich, sollte das Bruttogehalt (Nettogehalt + Steuern und Beiträge des Arbeitnehmers) veröffentlicht werden. [1] „Wissensvalorisierung“ ist der Prozess der Schaffung von sozialem und wirtschaftlichem Wert aus Wissen durch die Verknüpfung verschiedener Bereiche und Sektoren und durch die Umwandlung von Daten, Know-how und Forschungsergebnissen in nachhaltige Produkte, Dienstleistungen, Lösungen und wissensbasierte Maßnahmen zum Nutzen der Gesellschaft“ ( EUR-Lex – 32022H2415 – EN – EUR-Lex). Weitere Leitlinien zu bestimmten Bereichen der Valorisierung von Wissen finden sich in den Verhaltenskodizes der Europäischen Kommission zur Verwaltung geistiger Vermögenswerte, zur Normung, zur Ko-Kreation von Industrie und Hochschulen und zur Bürgerbeteiligung bei der Valorisierung von Wissen. [2] https://euraxess.ec.europa.eu/

titulo: Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI)
descricao_resumida: O Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) financia a verificação independente e validação de abordagens de computação quântica para operação em escala útil até 2033. O projeto estende o programa DARPA Underexplored Systems for Utility-Scale Quantum Computing (US2QC) e oferece validação terceirizada para organizações que buscam desenvolver computadores quânticos industriais. Trata-se de uma iniciativa de pesquisa focada em benchmarks quânticos e validação de viabilidade comercial.

In the simplest terms, the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI) seeks to determine whether it’s possible to build an industrially-useful computer by 2033. Specifically, QBI is designed to rigorously verify and validate whether any quantum computing approach can achieve utility-scale operation — meaning its computational value exceeds its cost.
QBI is not a competition between performers: DARPA is interested in evaluating all viable approaches for which there is available funding. Successful performers will progress through three stages:
In addition to funding performers, QBI will add value to their ongoing research and development efforts by providing unbiased third-party verification and validation of an organization’s path to a utility-scale quantum computer. QBI will also effectively communicate the results of this verification and validation effort to other U.S. government stakeholders.
QBI is an expansion of the existing DARPA Underexplored Systems for Utility-Scale Quantum Computing (US2QC). QBI is separate from but related to the existing Quantum Benchmarking (QB) program, which sought to determine the yardstick for impact.

descricao_completa:
Research Fellowship for researchers from Germany
    

    
    
        The NSTC (Taiwan) Research Fellowship supports you as a highly qualified postdoc or experienced researcher from Germany in conducting your research in Taiwan – regardless of discipline.
The Taiwanese NSTC funds up to two three- to twelve-month research stays annually; these stays can potentially be extended up to a total duration of three years. Applicants are pre-selected by the Humboldt Foundation.
The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation aims to achieve a good balance between genders and a high level of diversity among its fellows in all areas. We therefore expressly invite female scientists and members of underrepresented groups to apply.
We welcome all applications, regardless of ethnic, cultural or social background, gender identity, age, religion, worldview, disability or sexual orientation.
If you would like to apply for a NSTC (Taiwan) Research Fellowship, you will require an academic host who has previously received project funding from the National Science and Technology Council (NSTC), Taiwan. Individuals with whom you are in a close personal (marriage or civil partnership) or familial (parents, siblings, children) relationship cannot be selected as hosts.

What we offer
    

    
    
        The NSTC (Taiwan) Research Fellowship enables you to carry out your research in Taiwan in cooperation with a qualified academic host of your choice.
The monthly fellowship amount paid by NSTC is currently 85,000 NTD. During your stay abroad, the Humboldt Foundation will provide you with a contact person. We will also assist you in reintegrating in Germany: e.g. with allowances for job interviews or the possibility of a twelve-month return fellowship. We will keep in contact with you even after your research stay: Our alumni sponsorship measures flexibly support every Humboldtian’s individual journey through life, in both their career and their future collaborations.

descricao_completa:
Fellowship for gifted musicians and musicologists from Spain
    

    
    
        Gifted young musicians or musicologists from Spain are invited to apply for a Hezekiah WardweIl Fellowship from the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation.
In 1926–1928, Hezekiah C Wardwell (1877–1964) was one of the first ever fellowsof the previous Humboldt Foundation. On his passing, Wardwell left a significant sum of money to the Foundation that was to be used “to aid worthy Spanish students in gaining a musical education.” The philanthropist is said to have made this bequest to express his gratitude both to the Humboldt Foundation and to Spanish musicians who had helped him recover after an accident.

Our sponsorship
    

    
    
        The Wardwell Fellowship enables you to attend further training or an advanced degree programme at an academy of music or a conservatory in Germany. You may apply for funding for one or two semesters of study (from October to either February or July of the following year). The Humboldt Foundation awards up to ten Wardwell Fellowships a year.
You may spend part (up to five months) of a ten-month (two-semester) fellowshipin a different European country (except Spain) if this is necessary to pursue advanced studies.
The monthly fellowship grant is 900 euros. We additionally offer an initial lump sum of 250 euros and a travel allowance if you travel to Germany from Spain.

titulo: OP3424 - Pesquisa Aplicada para o Desenvolvimento de Sistema e Método de Recolhimento de Risers e Flowlines de Produção com Problemas de SCC-CO2 por Meio de Cabo de Recuperação, com Aplicação Interna e Externa
descricao_resumida: Contratar ICT, ICT em parceria com empresa, ou empresa brasileira para desenvolver pesquisa aplicada destinada à avaliação da viabilidade técnica, operacional e econômica de sistema e método para recolhimento de risers e flowlines de produção com problemas de SCC-CO2 por meio de cabo de recuperação, contemplando configurações com instalação interna e externa ao duto. descricao_completa: Desafio: O principal desafio tecnológico é viabilizar o recolhimento seguro e contínuo de risers e flowlines com problemas de SCC-CO2 em cenários nos quais a integridade estrutural residual do duto é incerta, variável ao longo do comprimento e potencialmente insuficiente para suportar os esforços de tração impostos pelos métodos convencionais de içamento e recolhimento. Nesses casos, a ruptura pode ocorrer de forma súbita, exigindo solução que preserve a continuidade mecânica da operação mesmo em situação de falha parcial da linha. Entre os desafios centrais do projeto está o dimensionamento do cabo de recuperação para assumir total ou predominantemente os esforços de tração, considerando contribuição axial residual nula ou desprezível do duto, bem como a definição de ancoragens e mecanismos de transferência de carga capazes de submeter o duto prioritariamente a compressão axial localizada na extremidade, e não a esforços distribuídos de tração ao longo de sua extensão. Também constitui desafio relevante a comparação técnica entre as arquiteturas com cabo interno e cabo externo. Na solução interna, devem ser avaliadas limitações de passagem no bore, irregularidades geométricas, ovalização, deposições, conectores internos, ausência de infraestrutura de lançamento e necessidade de instalação remota por ROV. Na solução externa, o desafio envolve garantir retenção adequada do cabo ao longo da linha, compatibilidade com transferência de carga, possibilidade de retenção de segmentos em caso de ruptura parcial e compatibilidade com o processo de bobinamento. Em águas profundas e ultraprofundas, os desafios operacionais são ampliados pela ação de correntes de fundo, pelo comportamento da catenária, pela variação contínua de carga durante a ascensão, pelas limitações de acesso remoto e pelas exigências de monitoramento e controle da operação. Soma-se a isso a necessidade de detalhar uma solução tecnicamente robusta, mas que priorize equipamentos já existentes na indústria submarina offshore, reduzindo adaptações, risco tecnológico, custo e prazo de implantação futura. Objetivo: Contratar ICT, ICT em parceria com empresa, ou empresa brasileira para desenvolver pesquisa aplicada destinada à avaliação da viabilidade técnica, operacional e econômica de sistema e método para recolhimento de risers e flowlines de produção com problemas de SCC-CO2 por meio de cabo de recuperação, contemplando configurações com instalação interna e externa ao duto. A Contratada deverá realizar levantamento do estado da arte aplicável ao recolhimento de linhas submarinas degradadas, identificar soluções existentes, lacunas, limitações e oportunidades, e, a partir disso, propor alternativas e arranjos para o desenvolvimento da solução. O projeto deverá contemplar a definição de requisitos funcionais, operacionais e de segurança; a caracterização de casos de referência; o cálculo das cargas principais no cabo, ancoragens, dispositivos auxiliares e interfaces com a embarcação; a comparação entre soluções com cabo interno e externo; a análise de viabilidade de inserção no bore e de retenção externa ao longo da linha; a definição conceitual do sistema, do método operacional e dos equipamentos necessários; e a análise técnico-econômica preliminar da rota mais promissora. Ao final, espera-se obter prova de conceito analítica em nível compatível com TRL-3 e roadmap estruturado de continuidade até TRL-9. Solução esperada: Espera-se obter, ao final do projeto, uma solução conceitualmente estruturada e analiticamente fundamentada para recolhimento de risers e flowlines de produção com problemas de SCC-CO2 por meio de cabo de recuperação, contemplando duas arquiteturas de aplicação: uma com cabo disposto internamente ao duto e outra com cabo disposto externamente ao longo da linha. A solução deverá incluir a definição de requisitos funcionais, operacionais e de segurança; casos de referência para aplicação; memória de cálculo das cargas principais; critérios de dimensionamento do cabo de recuperação; concepção das ancoragens e dos mecanismos de transferência de carga; definição dos dispositivos necessários à instalação do cabo, seja por pig, foam pig, pig bidirecional, crawler instrumentado, linha mensageira ou solução equivalente, seja por grampos, braçadeiras, cintas, colares bipartidos ou dispositivos externos instaláveis por ROV. Também se espera a descrição detalhada do método operacional de instalação, ancoragem, tração, monitoramento, controle, içamento e bobinamento, incluindo tratamento de eventos anômalos, limites operacionais, respostas a variações bruscas de carga e estratégias para manutenção da continuidade operacional em caso de ruptura parcial. A solução deverá ainda identificar os equipamentos e subsistemas necessários, tais como cabo de recuperação, sistemas de acionamento de carretel, guinchos, tensionadores, polias, guias, sensores, interfaces com embarcação, ferramentas de ROV e elementos de proteção e armazenamento. A entrega esperada não é um protótipo físico nesta fase, mas uma prova de conceito analítica compatível com TRL-3, acompanhada de avaliação técnico-econômica preliminar, recomendação da rota mais promissora e roadmap de desenvolvimento até TRL-9, incluindo testes, qualificação, piloto offshore, implantação e estimativa paramétrica de prazo e custo.

The U.S. National Science Foundation offers postdoctoral fellows paid opportunities to expand their skills and knowledge in science and engineering. This page highlights opportunities that postdoctoral fellows can directly apply to. If you're interested in supporting postdocs with NSF funding, explore NSF's Funding Search page. Most of NSF's funding opportunities allow proposers to include postdocs in their project budget. NSF's Engineering Fellows program supports independent postdoctoral research in engineering. In addition to hands-on academic research with a faculty advisor, each fellowship cohort participates in professional development and mentoring activities designed to prepare them for future research careers. These two-year fellowships provide a stipend and travel allowance. Citizens and permanent residents of the United States who have recently earned a Ph.D. are eligible to apply. The program accepts applications on an annual basis. Visit the eFellows website to learn more. Funded by NSF, the Innovative Postdoctoral Entrepreneurial Research Fellowship (I-PERF) recruits, trains, mentors, matches and funds early-career, Ph.D.-level scientists and engineers so they can participate in innovative entrepreneurial activities at some of the nation’s most promising startup companies. Fellows receive an annual stipend of $78,000, optional individual health and life insurance benefits, relocation assistance to the approved host company, a professional conference travel allowance, and scripted professional development training. Applicants must have earned a doctoral degree in an NSF-supported STEM discipline within the last seven years. Only U.S. citizens, nationals or permanent residents are eligible to apply. See the I-PERF website for full eligibility criteria. Visit the I-PERF website to apply. The NSF Mathematical and Physical Sciences Directorate (NSF MPS) offers three postdoctoral fellowship programs: NSF Mathematical and Physical Sciences Ascending Postdoctoral Research Fellowships Supports postdoctoral fellows performing impactful research across all fields supported by NSF MPS while broadening the participation of groups that are underrepresented in the mathematical and physical sciences. NSF Mathematical Sciences Postdoctoral Research Fellowships Supports postdoctoral fellows in pursuing research and training in mathematics and statistics, including their applications to other disciplines. NSF Astronomy and Astrophysics Postdoctoral Fellowships Supports postdoctoral fellows to conduct an integrated program of independent research and education in areas supported by the NSF Division of Astronomical Sciences. NSF's Postdoctoral Research Fellowships support independent postdoctoral research, allowing fellows to perform work that will broaden their perspectives, facilitate interdisciplinary interactions, and help establish them in leadership positions. These two- or three-year fellowships provide a stipend and a research and training allowance. Citizens, nationals and permanent residents of the United States who have recently earned a Ph.D. or will have earned their Ph.D. before beginning the fellowship are eligible to apply. Current postdoctoral fellowship opportunities can be found on NSF's Funding Search. Deadlines vary by program: some accept proposals at any time while others have annual deadlines. titulo: 5ª Chamada Pública Conjunta - Finep e Conselho Norueguês de Pesquisa (RCN)
descricao_resumida: O Conselho Norueguês de Pesquisa (RCN) e a Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep) instituem a quinta chamada pública conjunta Finep-RCN em 2026, para apoio de projetos a serem iniciados em 2027, com a observância dos termos e procedimentos adiante estabelecidos. Alinhados com o acordo BN21 (Brasil-Noruega Século XXI), a Finep e o RCN lançam esta chamada conjunta com vistas a aumentar a colaboração entre a Noruega e o Brasil por meio de parcerias entre instituições científicas e tecnológicas
descricao_completa: O Conselho Norueguês de Pesquisa (RCN) e a Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (Finep) instituem a quinta chamada pública conjunta Finep-RCN em 2026, para apoio de projetos a serem iniciados em 2027, com a observância dos termos e procedimentos adiante estabelecidos. Alinhados com o acordo BN21 (Brasil-Noruega Século XXI), a Finep e o RCN lançam esta chamada conjunta com vistas a aumentar a colaboração entre a Noruega e o Brasil por meio de parcerias entre instituições científicas e tecnológicas e empresas de ambos os países para o desenvolvimento de produtos, processos e serviços inovadores com potencial de comercialização nas áreas de Petróleo, Energia Ambientalmente Amigável e Transporte Marítimo Verde. A iniciativa integra a Rede Eureka, a maior rede pública internacional de cooperação em pesquisa e inovação, presente em mais de 45 países. O processo seletivo de que trata esta CHAMADA PÚBLICA CONJUNTA é divido em duas etapas: Internacional e Nacional. Os critérios da Etapa Internacional são apresentados no sítio eletrônico da Rede Eureka. Na Etapa Internacional, os consórcios deverão submeter a proposta completa em inglês por meio da plataforma Eureka. Os projetos serão avaliados conjuntamente pela Finep e pelo RCN quanto à elegibilidade, mérito técnico-científico, potencial de mercado, impactos econômicos, sociais e ambientais, qualidade das parcerias e viabilidade de execução. As propostas aprovadas receberão o Selo Eureka. Na Etapa Nacional, apenas os projetos contemplados com o Selo Eureka poderão apresentar à Finep o detalhamento da parcela brasileira do projeto, em português, por meio da Plataforma de Apoio e Financiamento .    Os recursos da Finep serão direcionados às ICTs brasileiras participantes dos projetos. As empresas atuarão como parceiras cofinanciadoras, realizando aportes financeiros e/ou não financeiros equivalentes a, no mínimo, 20% do valor total da proposta.   Do lado norueguês, o RCN apoiará as ICTs norueguesas.   Cronograma   Etapa Internacional Prazo para conclusão do cadastro das instituições brasileiras na Plataforma de Apoio e Financiamento da Finep: 9 de setembro de 2026; Prazo para submissão da proposta na plataforma Eureka: 16 de setembro de 2026; Decisão conjunta Finep/RCN e divulgação dos projetos contemplados com o Selo Eureka: 6 de novembro de 2026.   Etapa Nacional Início do envio das propostas nacionais à Finep: 9 de novembro de 2026; Prazo final para submissão: 16 de dezembro de 2026; Divulgação do resultado final: 26 de fevereiro de 2027. O documento “Instruções para as ICTS e Empresas Brasileiras - Anexo Finep – Etapa Internacional”, presente na lista de documentos abaixo, traz o detalhamento da Chamada Pública Conjunta no que diz respeito às condições de apoio da Finep às ICTs e as empresas brasileiras.   Quaisquer dúvidas podem ser esclarecidas através do e-mail: cp_Eureka_Brasil-Noruega@finep.gov.br

titulo: OP3441 - Absorção - equilíbrio termodinâmico e processos de desidratação e adoçamento de gás natural
descricao_resumida: Objetivo Elucidar as causas da perda de desempenho de solventes na desidratação e adoçamento de gás natural, usando a planta piloto e equipamentos de caracterização dos solventes, bem como a montagem de um equipamento para investigação experimental sobre o equilíbrio líquido-vapor de misturas contendo glicóis, e uso destes dados na melhora da exatidão de equações de estado pertinentes.
descricao_completa: Desafio: - Captura de CO2 de gás natural em unidade de produção offshore; - Desidratação de gás natural em unidades de produção offshore; - Espaço ocupado pelos sistemas de processamento de gás. Objetivo: Elucidar as causas da perda de desempenho de solventes na desidratação e adoçamento de gás natural, usando a planta piloto e equipamentos de caracterização dos solventes, bem como a montagem de um equipamento para investigação experimental sobre o equilíbrio líquido-vapor de misturas contendo glicóis, e uso destes dados na melhora da exatidão de equações de estado pertinentes. Solução esperada: Desenvolver metodologia para envelhecimento de solventes; Desenvolver metodologia para caracterização físico-química de absorventes; construir planta piloto de absorção em escala banca, com coluna de absorção e coluna de regeneração; Desenvolver um protocolo de operação da planta piloto de captura de CO2 para envelhecimento de solvente; Metodologias teórico-computacionais para a previsão do desempenho de solventes usados na captura de CO2 e desidratação de gás natural; Desenvolver metodologia para a aferição do teor glicóis na fase gasosa; Obter dados de ELV de sistemas formados por água, CO2, CH4, componentes do gás natural e glicóis; Construir uma rotina de simulação de desidratação por absorção com glicóis, como MEG, DEG e TEG em Hysys usando a modelagem termodinâmica.

titulo: OP3478 - Gaseificação de resíduos sólidos urbanos (RSU) para a produção de gás de síntese
descricao_resumida: Objetivo Desenvolver e validar, em escala piloto, um processo de gaseificação de combustível derivado de resíduos (CDR) produzido a partir de resíduos sólidos urbanos (RSU) representativos da região de Três Lagoas (MS) para a obtenção de gás de síntese (CO + H2) com composição adequada ao processamento em planta de síntese de amônia, abrangendo os aspectos operacionais e técnicos do processo.
descricao_completa: Desafio: A crescente geração de resíduos sólidos urbanos (RSU) representa um desafio ambiental e de gestão significativo em escala global. A disposição inadequada em aterros sanitários acarreta problemas como a contaminação do solo e da água, emissão de gases de efeito estufa (principalmente metano) e a ocupação de grandes áreas. A destinação exclusiva dos resíduos ao aterro sanitário, por sua vez, resulta na subutilização do potencial energético desses materiais. O processo de gaseificação de RSU propõe uma abordagem tecnológica avançada, voltada para a conversão do passivo ambiental representado pelos RSU em combustível derivado de resíduos (CDR) de elevada qualidade. A Unidade de Fertilizantes Nitrogenados III (UFN-III), em Três Lagoas (MS), reúne condições estratégicas para a instalação de uma planta de gaseificação de RSU para a obtenção de gás de síntese. A escolha se justifica por sua ampla área, alto consumo de gás natural (2,2 milhões Nm³/dia) e a proximidade a diversas fontes de biomassa. O potencial de geração de gás de síntese (CO + H2) a partir do RSU deste município pode substituir até 30% do gás natural (GN) processado diariamente na UFN-III, segundo estimativas internas, o que geraria um expressivo benefício econômico, por redução de OPEX, para a Companhia. Assim, as gerências CENPES/PDIPL/GPQF e PDP/IP-LOG-MID-REN/PROJ-UFN-III estabeleceram a linha de pesquisa intitulada ¿Avaliação da produção de gás de síntese a partir da gaseificação de resíduos sólidos urbanos para a UFN-III¿. O objetivo do estudo é realizar a avaliação técnica, em escala piloto, de um sistema de gaseificação de RSU para a obtenção de gás de síntese a ser processado em uma planta de síntese de amônia, em substituição parcial do GN. Com este projeto, as gerências citadas pretendem validar o processo de gaseificação em escala piloto, bem como identificar os riscos técnicos e operacionais inerentes à implantação comercial deste processo. Assim, a gerência CENPES/PDIPL/GPQF busca parceria estratégica com uma Instituição Científica e Tecnológica (ICT) que possua comprovado domínio tecnológico no processo de gaseificação de CDR para celebração de um Termo de Cooperação (TC). As etapas e as principais atividades a serem desenvolvidas pela ICT seguem abaixo: 1- Caracterização, definição de rotas tecnológicas e produção experimental de CDR: diagnóstico técnico e amostragem sazonal dos RSU; caracterização físico-química e energética dos RSU e do CDR; consolidação de infraestrutura analítica. 2- Validação Operacional e Simulação Avançada: planejamento e execução dos ensaios de gaseificação em planta piloto; monitoramento, controle e otimização dos parâmetros operacionais para maximizar os percentuais de CO + H2 e reduzir contaminantes no gás de síntese; modelagem numérica, CFD e calibração do modelo digital. A fim de garantir o pleno cumprimento das etapas do plano de trabalho e assim, alcançar os resultados esperados, a ICT parceira deve atender de forma integral às seguintes premissas: 1) A ICT deve ser uma universidade com equipe técnica de comprovada capacitação na tecnologia de gaseificação; 2) A unidade piloto deve ser um ativo da ICT (universidade) a ser selecionada; 3) A unidade piloto deve ser projetada para o processamento de CDR proveniente de RSU; 4) A capacidade mínima de processamento da unidade piloto deve ser de 250 kg/h de CDR; 5) A equipe técnica deve ter comprovada capacitada em desenvolvimento e calibração de modelos computacionais multifásicos avançados (CFD) a partir dos dados gerados em testes na unidade piloto para aumento de escala visando a um reator industrial para a UFN III. 6) A solução esperada deve alcançar, no mínimo, TRL 6 e CRL 5. Objetivo: Desenvolver e validar, em escala piloto, um processo de gaseificação de combustível derivado de resíduos (CDR) produzido a partir de resíduos sólidos urbanos (RSU) representativos da região de Três Lagoas (MS) para a obtenção de gás de síntese (CO + H2) com composição adequada ao processamento em planta de síntese de amônia, abrangendo os aspectos operacionais e técnicos do processo. Solução esperada: Validação técnica e operacional, em escala piloto, do processo de gaseificação de combustível derivado de resíduos (CDR) produzido a partir de resíduos sólidos urbanos (RSU) representativos da região de Três Lagoas - MS, para a obtenção de gás de síntese (CO + H2). Os dados gerados durante as corridas devem viabilizar a calibração e a validação de um modelo computacional multifásico avançado, reduzindo as incertezas de CAPEX e OPEX na elaboração de um projeto básico de reator industrial para a UFN-III. É desejável que a ICT avalie a mitigação de emissões, expressa em toneladas de CO2 equivalente por tonelada de CDR processada (tCO2e/t CDR), como indicador de desempenho das rotas de gaseificação voltadas à produção de energia e de insumos para fertilizantes. Espera-se que a solução esperada alcance, no mínimo, TRL 6 e CRL 5.
